summary: Research + independently verify worldwide government heavy-metal limits for infant/child foods, per jurisdiction

confirmed.product_scope: Infant formula, formula for special medical purposes intended for infants and follow-up formula
confirmed.basis: 0.01 mg/kg. Portion: Whole commodity; note states 'The ML applies to the formula as consumed' (i.e. reconstituted/ready-to-feed). No powder-vs-liquid or cow-milk-vs-soy distinction. Relevant commodity standards CXS 72-1981 and CXS 156-1987.
confirmed.article_ref: CXS 193-1995 Schedule I, LEAD table, entry 'Infant formula, formula for special medical purposes intended for infants and follow-up formula' (current/Rev.2024)
confirmed.note: Verbatim match in the current CXS 193 (amended 1997-2024): 0.01 mg/kg = 10 ug/kg, 'Whole commodity', 'The ML applies to the formula as consumed', CXS 72-1981 & 156-1987. Independently corroborated in the ISDI-hosted 2019 consolidated official text (identical entry). The 0.01 value replaced the pre-2014 0.02; older FAO fileadmin copies still show 0.02 and are stale.

confirmed.product_scope: Cereal-based foods for infants and young children (up to 12 months and 12-36 months)
confirmed.basis: 0.02 mg/kg. Portion: 'Whole commodity as sold; not reconstituted or otherwise prepared for consumption' (as-sold basis). Relevant commodity standard CXS 74-1981.
confirmed.article_ref: CXS 193-1995 Schedule I, LEAD table, entry 'Cereal-based foods for infants and young children' (current/Rev.2024)
confirmed.note: Verbatim match in current CXS 193: 0.02 mg/kg = 20 ug/kg, 'Whole commodity as sold; not reconstituted or otherwise prepared for consumption', CXS 74-1981. This entry was ADDED after 2019 (absent from the 2019 consolidated text); CCCF15 (2022) forwarded 0.02 mg/kg 'as is' for lead in cereal-based foods for infants and young children, adopted at CAC45 Step 5/8. Minor caveat: the standard's basis is 'as sold / not reconstituted', NOT 'dry-matter basis' as the claim's parenthetical gloss implies — the dry-matter basis applies to the DON mycotoxin ML for this category, not the lead ML. Value/scope/as-sold basis all confirmed.

confirmed.product_scope: Ready-to-eat meals for infants and young children (up to 12 months and 12-36 months); corresponds to canned baby foods CXS 73-1981
confirmed.basis: 0.02 mg/kg. Portion: 'Whole commodity' (ready-to-eat / as consumed). Relevant commodity standard CXS 73-1981.
confirmed.article_ref: CXS 193-1995 Schedule I, LEAD table, entry 'Ready-to-eat meals for infants and young children' (current/Rev.2024)
confirmed.note: Verbatim match in current CXS 193: 0.02 mg/kg = 20 ug/kg, 'Whole commodity', ML applies to all ready-to-eat meals for infants (up to 12 mo) and young children (12-36 mo), relevant standard CXS 73-1981 (Canned Baby Foods) - confirming the claim's canned-baby-foods correspondence. Added after 2019: CCCF15 (2022) forwarded 0.02 mg/kg to CAC45 at Step 5, finalized at CCCF16 (2023)/CAC46 (2023).

confirmed.product_scope: Fruit juices (whole commodity or reconstituted to original concentration, ready-to-drink; also applies to nectars; note explicitly extends ML to fruit juices for infants and young children)

confirmed.article_ref: CXS 193-1995 Schedule I, LEAD table, entry 'Fruit juices' (current/Rev.2024)
confirmed.note: Verbatim match, including the claimed note: current CXS 193 shows 0.03 mg/kg = 30 ug/kg, reconstituted-to-original ready-to-drink basis, applies to nectars, does NOT apply to juices exclusively from berries/small fruit, CXS 247-2005, and the exact note 'The ML also applies to fruit juices for infants and young children.' Value/basis also corroborated in the 2019 ISDI text (the infant note was added in a later amendment and is present in the current version).

confirmed.product_scope: Grape juice (whole commodity or reconstituted to original concentration, ready-to-drink; also applies to nectars; note explicitly extends ML to fruit juices for infants and young children)
